marker_text: // Hard-won: f870729d: relative export paths were searched one directory above the agent working directory.
defect: read_file passes the workspace parent as the worker root for relative paths, although the agent works inside the primary repository. Files created by the agent are therefore looked up in the wrong directory.
trigger: Agent writes report.txt in its repository, then caller exports report.txt.
match_rule: Must identify relative export resolving against workspace_root rather than the primary repository/agent cwd and causing wrong-file or missing-file results.
near_misses: Diff export formatting; path traversal speculation; branch pushing.
why_findable: The same change adds primary_repository_path for git operations and exposes the repository layout used by read_file.

marker_text: // Hard-won: f870729d: relative export paths were searched one directory above the agent working directory.
defect: File upload sends layout.workspace_root as --root, placing a relative file outside the agent primary repository. An acknowledged upload consequently does not appear where the agent works.
trigger: Upload config.txt to a session whose primary repository is a child of workspace_root.
match_rule: Must identify uploaded relative files landing at workspace root instead of primary repository cwd.
near_misses: Missing upload cancellation; export-only reads; general path validation.
why_findable: The upload change explicitly uses the export layout; the existing primary repository resolver shows the distinct agent location.
notes: Same marker/fix also protects read root; this record covers the independently introduced write path.

marker_text: // Hard-won: 5dafd135: a withdrawn startup prompt was still submitted after the worker attached.
defect: A prompt waits for a starting session without registering cancellation with interrupt_turn. An interrupt while it waits cannot withdraw it, so worker attachment later submits unwanted work.
trigger: Submit prompt before worker attachment, interrupt session, then attach worker.
match_rule: Must connect readiness-held prompt to interrupt failing to withdraw it and subsequent unwanted submission.
near_misses: Readiness timeout length; ordinary running-turn cancellation.
why_findable: The new readiness loop and existing interrupt handler are both visible and have no shared withdrawal state.

marker_text: // Hard-won: f67ed023: Haiku inherited an invalid effort from a sibling model and never ran its first prompt
defect: Child effort validation and inheritance use chosen.choices from the profile default model rather than the selected child model. A child can receive an unsupported effort and fail startup.
trigger: Parent uses high effort; spawn another model in the same profile whose effort catalog excludes high.
match_rule: Must identify validating/inheriting efforts from profile default instead of selected model and unsupported setting reaching child.
near_misses: Quota ranking or model visibility alone.
why_findable: Candidate choices identify their default model and model-specific discovery exists in the repository.

marker_text: // Hard-won: 3c668c3d: one SQLITE_BUSY recorder failure terminated the native API server.
defect: A database recording error propagates out of record_activity_stream; that future participates in the API server select, so a transient SQLite write failure terminates the whole server.
location: mj-cli/src/server/api_activity.rs, record_activity_stream, lines 37-45; server run select
trigger: Activity snapshot changes while a competing writer causes SQLITE_BUSY.
match_rule: Must connect activity recording failure propagation to termination of the serving API future.
near_misses: Only quota cache contention or missing activity history.
why_findable: The change adds both the fallible recorder and the select arm that lets it stop serving.

marker_text: // Hard-won: 55b8ea7: provider catalog and discovered model rows evicted each other from SQLite
defect: Provider catalog bodies are stored using the empty model key in profile_config_cache, which discovery already uses for default-model configurations. Each writer replaces the other payload, so cached catalog fallback can disappear after normal discovery.
trigger: Fetch catalog, discover profile default model, then launch while catalog provider is unavailable.
match_rule: Must identify catalog and discovered profile configuration sharing the same profile/empty-model database row and overwriting each other.
near_misses: Cache refresh interval; duplicate TOML catalog key; generic network failure.
why_findable: The new cache calls and existing table key/discovery writes expose the collision without third-party facts.

marker_text: // Hard-won: 767a0c57: a streamed commit between frontier and transcript reads made a valid projection fail session loading.
defect: The windowed loader reads the committed frontier and mutable transcript in separate autocommit SELECTs. A concurrent commit can make transcript bodies newer than the frontier, producing an inconsistent projection that fails session loading.
trigger: Worker journal projection commits between frontier and transcript SELECTs while daemon polls.
match_rule: Must identify missing read transaction across frontier and transcript/window reads and resulting inconsistent generation under concurrent writes.
near_misses: Only excess history loading or transcript window size.
why_findable: The new loader performs successive reads on a Connection while projection writes are transactional elsewhere in the repository.

marker_text: // Hard-won: 924190f: a cache reaper removed a pinned worker source and sessions failed until restart
defect: The daemon returns its startup-pinned local worker path without checking it still exists or resolving another source. If that build-cache path is removed, subsequent session starts repeatedly fail until daemon restart although a usable source may exist.
trigger: Cache cleanup removes pinned local binary while daemon continues running; create another session.
match_rule: Must identify lifetime-cached local path surviving file deletion and preventing fresh worker resolution/session startup.
near_misses: Worker version mismatch or repeated hashing cost alone.
why_findable: The pin stores a filesystem path and returns it directly; source-resolution alternatives are visible.

marker_text: // Hard-won: 2980a9b9: web feed projection self-deadlocked on lifecycle state and hung the daemon.
defect: active_lifecycles now acquires the controller mutex, but session_projection already holds that mutex while calling it. Publishing the web feed re-locks a non-reentrant mutex and hangs the daemon.
trigger: Publish session_projection for the web viewer.
match_rule: Must identify session_projection holding controller lock when active_lifecycles attempts the same lock, causing self-deadlock.
near_misses: Generic lock order inversion involving another thread or slow rendering.
why_findable: The new lock and existing call chain are in the same daemon module.

marker_text: // Hard-won: 66888613: a temporary recovery-copy refusal delayed capture and produced an empty review
defect: The new early CaptureDelta runs before background recovery settles. A temporary lifecycle refusal is silently converted to captured=None, so preparation chooses a reviewer before retrying capture; even a turn with no changes then blocks its prompts on slow or non-returning reviewer discovery instead of finishing without a reviewer.
trigger: Recovery copy reserves the session during early capture of a no-change turn; automatic reviewer discovery is slow or does not return.
match_rule: Must identify temporary lifecycle/recovery refusal of early CaptureDelta being ignored before expensive reviewer resolution, delaying or hanging an empty review and its prompt hold; retry/wait must happen before choosing reviewer.
near_misses: Reviewer selection failures unrelated to capture; claims of changed-file review coverage being lost without explaining this ordering.
why_findable: The prior resolve_after_background_work helper and the new capture before it reveal inconsistent lease handling.
notes: Lower-priority candidate: demonstrated runtime consequence is unnecessary prompt blocking on reviewer discovery, not lost changed-file coverage. Historical regression deliberately hangs reviewer resolution to demonstrate the missing capture retry.

marker_text: // Hard-won: 15867df0: GitHub tokens were exposed in container argv.
defect: Container provisioning embeds the full GitHub token in --env GH_TOKEN=... arguments. The token becomes visible through process argument inspection and command diagnostics rather than remaining private credential input.
trigger: Launch a managed container with a discovered GitHub token.
match_rule: Must identify the literal GitHub token entering container/SSH process argv and exposure to process listings or command logs.
near_misses: Generic token persistence inside the intended container; authentication failure; URL rewriting.
why_findable: The diff formats the secret into extra_run_args, and target process execution consumes those arguments directly.

marker_text: // Hard-won: ed3e0b29: Stop failed after a successful worker kill because grep matched itself.
defect: The new leftover check runs ps piped to grep -F with the worker-match string in grep argv. ps can include that grep process, so a successful stop reports worker still running and fails teardown.
trigger: Stop an absent or successfully killed bare-target worker while ps observes the checking grep.
match_rule: Must identify grep process argv containing its own fixed search string, causing false leftover detection and failed stop.
near_misses: The main PID scan matching unrelated workers; ETXTBSY during replacement.
why_findable: The new shell pipeline exposes both the process listing and the search process arguments.

marker_text: // Hard-won: 3002b626: macOS destroy failed when awk -v received a newline.
defect: hel_tree_running passes the multiline process tree directly as an awk -v assignment. The macOS awk rejects newline-containing assignment values, so stopping a worker with descendants fails during its liveness check and prevents destroy cleanup.
trigger: Destroy a bare macOS session whose worker tree contains multiple processes.
match_rule: Must identify multiline hel_tree passed via awk -v and macOS awk rejection breaking stop/destroy.
near_misses: Process group membership mistakes; inability to find ps.
why_findable: The shell constructs newline-separated tree records and invokes platform awk; macOS is an explicit supported target in repository code.

marker_text: // Hard-won: 1eefcdfc: restore through a staged-home symlink could overwrite the user's profile.
defect: The upgrade creates worker_root/profile symlinks to users original harness homes, but resume cleanup leaves that symlink intact before checkpoint restore writes into profile. Restoring into a reused local root can overwrite the users own profile instead of a private staged home.
trigger: Upgrade an existing local session, then restore a checkpoint into its reused worker root with the linked profile directory.
match_rule: Must connect newly created profile symlink, restore into reused local worker root, and writes following the link into users profile due to missing unlink.
near_misses: Only skills-sync following links or ordinary staged-home deletion.
why_findable: The diff introduces the symlink migration while existing clear_relay_state_plan and checkpoint restore retain/write the same profile path.

marker_text: // Hard-won: 26ae8304: a reserved workspace name returned 500 for caller error.
defect: The new database refusal of the empty default workspace propagates through the create_workspace handler as an internal error. A caller-controlled reserved name receives HTTP 500 with a log reference instead of a bad-request response explaining how to correct the name.
trigger: POST /api/v1/workspaces with name default on an instance whose built-in default workspace has no sessions.
match_rule: Must identify reserved default-name refusal being raised as backend/internal HTTP 500 instead of client error with usable explanation.
near_misses: Whether default should be listed; lack of workspace selection at session creation.
why_findable: The new store ensure error and existing handler ? conversion into ApiFailure are both visible at introduction.

marker_text: // Hard-won: d92ab7ce: the lifecycle UPDATE omitted build_cache_json and live sessions reloaded without their mounted cache
defect: The new field-owned lifecycle UPDATE omits build_cache_json even though provisioning resolves build_cache and persists it via that lifecycle writer. Reloaded sessions lose their mounted build-cache configuration.
trigger: Provision session with build cache then reload daemon state.
match_rule: Must identify build_cache missing from lifecycle persistence despite being set during provisioning, causing reload/resume to lose it.
near_misses: Other stale full-record fields, additional mounts or container CPU settings.
why_findable: Provisioning assignments, SessionRecord field and new UPDATE are available together at introduction.
notes: The lifecycle UPDATE predates this bug; introduction adds build_cache and the provisioning assignment but omits the necessary lifecycle writer column.

marker_text: // Hard-won: a3fd1514: consecutive Ctrl-K presses discarded earlier killed lines.
defect: Each kill overwrites kill_buffer, including consecutive Ctrl-K operations. Killing a line and its newline leaves only the newline available to Ctrl-Y.
location: src/hel_chat.rs: kill_range/kill_to_line_end and Ctrl-K/Ctrl-Y handlers (locate by function names in saved intro diff)
trigger: At the start of line1\nline2 press Ctrl-K twice and Ctrl-Y.
match_rule: Identify consecutive Ctrl-K overwriting earlier killed text and Ctrl-Y consequently failing to restore the complete killed block.
near_misses: Other cursor movement or word-delete semantics.
why_findable: The diff adds both the overwriting kill buffer and Ctrl-K/Ctrl-Y handlers; the loss follows directly from their composition.
notes: base is intro^; attribution inspected in saved fix and intro diffs. Marker may have been added after fix.

marker_text: // Hard-won: 6c06003: OSC window-title payloads leaked into rendered transcripts
defect: The sanitizer only consumes CSI escapes. For OSC it drops ESC and BEL but emits the printable window-title payload into the transcript.
trigger: Render tool output containing ESC ] 0 ; title BEL followed by normal output.
match_rule: Identify OSC/string escape payloads remaining visible because only CSI is consumed.
near_misses: General ANSI styling support or a claim that escape sequences execute in the terminal.
why_findable: The added sanitizer and its callers process arbitrary terminal output; the non-CSI branch demonstrably preserves the payload.
notes: base is intro^; attribution inspected in saved fix and intro diffs. Marker may have been added after fix.

marker_text: // Hard-won: aa4e0b51: OpenSSH used Mjolnir accept-new before the user's strict host-key requirement.
defect: The helper puts StrictHostKeyChecking=accept-new before user SSH options. OpenSSH uses the first supplied value, so an explicit strict policy in ssh_args is ignored and an unknown key is accepted.
trigger: Configure ssh_args with -o StrictHostKeyChecking=yes and connect to an unknown host.
match_rule: Identify default-first SSH option ordering overriding explicit StrictHostKeyChecking=yes and accepting previously unknown host keys.
near_misses: Complaints about accept-new alone, password prompts, or connection timeout duration.
why_findable: The diff shows argument order and the user option extension; OpenSSH option precedence is stable external behavior.
notes: base is intro^; attribution inspected in saved fix and intro diffs. Marker may have been added after fix.

marker_text: // Hard-won: 987af2e4b4: an open transcript kept stale Unicode glyphs after symbol mode changed.
defect: The change makes transcript glyphs depend on a mutable symbol set without adding that set to the transcript row-cache invalidation condition. An open transcript reuses Unicode rows after switching to ASCII.
trigger: Draw a transcript, change Setup Symbols to ASCII without changing width/theme/render mode, and redraw.
match_rule: Identify stale transcript rows across a symbol-set change due to the cache omitting that dependency.
near_misses: Hard-coded glyphs outside the cached transcript or missing theme-color invalidation.
why_findable: The diff changes glyph production and provides symbol configuration while existing cache invalidation is visible in the same repository.
notes: base is intro^; attribution inspected in saved fix and intro diffs. Marker may have been added after fix.

defect: New direct workspace Rename/Close shortcuts open a manager subview, but Escape/Cancel resets that subview to the manager list. The user is taken to a screen absent from the navigation path.
location: mj-tui/src/workspaces.rs: open_workspace_command and handle_workspace_manager_key, lines 550-575 and 730-745
trigger: From the dashboard invoke direct workspace Rename or Close, then Escape.
match_rule: Identify direct shortcut dismissal returning to the Workspaces list instead of the dashboard it came from.

why_findable: The diff adds the direct shortcut entry path and retains unconditional subview-to-list dismissal.

marker_text: // Hard-won: 11f841e4: shortcut Rename completion returned to an unopened manager
defect: New direct workspace Rename/Close shortcuts reuse completion handling that resets finished mutations to the manager list. A successful direct action unexpectedly opens the Workspaces manager.

match_rule: Identify successful direct Rename or Close completion navigating to the manager list instead of returning to the dashboard.
near_misses: Escape/Cancel behavior alone or mutation failures.

marker_text: // Hard-won: fb0622d0f159: searching “rend” ranked Resize above the literal rendering match.
defect: All non-prefix label matches share one score tier. Multiple word-start bonuses can make a scattered subsequence outrank a contiguous literal substring, putting Resize pane down above Toggle transcript rendering for rend.
trigger: Search the command palette for rend.
match_rule: Identify scattered word-start subsequence matching outranking a contiguous label substring, with a concrete consequence for palette ordering.
near_misses: Selected-row retention, description-only matches, or general requests for better fuzzy search.
why_findable: The scoring and command labels are present; the scores can be evaluated directly from the diff.
notes: base is intro^; attribution inspected in saved fix and intro diffs. Marker may have been added after fix.

marker_text: // Hard-won: b6b9787: this session's prompts appeared interleaved with other sessions' history
defect: Project-history query results are flattened to text without preserving session ownership. History navigation walks other sessions interleaved with this session instead of exhausting this session first.
trigger: Reopen a session in a project whose prompts alternate between two sessions and press Up repeatedly.
match_rule: Identify loss of session grouping in prefetched navigation history and other sessions appearing before older prompts from this session.
near_misses: Reverse search scope or database query latency.
why_findable: The added move_history project query drops PromptHistoryEntry.session_id, and the chronological query and session identity are visible at intro.
notes: base is intro^; attribution inspected in saved fix and intro diffs. Marker may have been added after fix.

marker_text: // Hard-won: db7d3a78: --json export with --out printed prose instead of a JSON object.
defect: The new export command accepts --json but its byte-export file path calls write_bytes, which unconditionally prints a prose confirmation. JSON consumers cannot parse stdout when --out is supplied.
trigger: Run mj export --session ID --json --out result.patch.
match_rule: Identify --json being ignored for export with --out and prose appearing on stdout.
near_misses: Raw byte output without --out or JSON formatting on unrelated commands.
why_findable: The flag, dispatch and printing helper are all added in the same diff.
notes: base is intro^; attribution inspected in saved fix and intro diffs. Marker may have been added after fix.

marker_text: // Hard-won: af22566c: rebuilding the environment from login exports dropped required container image variables
defect: Worker bootstrap reconstructs a minimal login environment and re-execs with env_clear. Container image ENV values absent from login startup scripts are dropped, changing toolchain and preinstalled-tool locations.
trigger: Start a container worker whose image defines RUSTUP_HOME or PLAYWRIGHT_BROWSERS_PATH only with ENV.
match_rule: Identify clearing container image ENV during clean login re-exec and consequent loss of required tool configuration.
near_misses: Host environment leakage, credential filtering, or ordinary target_environment override precedence.
why_findable: The diff adds env_clear and minimal discovery; image installation/environment declarations exist in the repository at intro.
notes: base is intro^; attribution inspected in saved fix and intro diffs. Marker may have been added after fix.

marker_text: // Hard-won: 20b5749a: an open popup let a click activate the control it covered.
defect: Popup rectangles are added to ordinary reverse-registration hit testing. A later registered field underneath an open dropdown wins over the visually covering popup, activating the wrong control.
trigger: Open a combobox whose popup overlaps a later registered field, then click a popup row over that field.
match_rule: Identify hit testing prioritizing underlying later controls over an open popup, causing the wrong control to receive clicks.
near_misses: Keyboard navigation or popup placement/clipping alone.
why_findable: The diff adds popup_area to the same hit predicate as ordinary area, and rendering paints the popup over the fields.
notes: base is intro^; attribution inspected in saved fix and intro diffs. Marker may have been added after fix.

marker_text: // Hard-won: eef1275: a project-step redraw dropped the current path suggestion reply on slow machines.
defect: Completion state and in-flight replies belong to a particular input DOM element. Project catalog loading rebuilds the step, so a current reply fails the activeElement check against the removed input and suggestions disappear.
trigger: Hold the project catalog response; type a path to request completion; finish catalog loading before returning completion.
match_rule: Identify input replacement on step redraw invalidating an otherwise current path-completion response due to element-local state/focus checks.
near_misses: Dropping genuinely stale prefixes, debounce timing, or backend completion errors.
why_findable: The diff adds element-owned asynchronous completion; existing step render signatures and catalog redraw behavior are available at intro.
notes: base is intro^; attribution inspected in saved fix and intro diffs. Marker may have been added after fix.

marker_text: // Hard-won: 94305629: a never-prompted archived session was offered a resume that always failed.
defect: The new wiki-session command unconditionally recommends resume --wiki for archived records. An archive with no user prompt cannot form a restoration turn, so the recommended command always fails.
trigger: Destroy a session before sending any prompt, then inspect it with mj sessions --session WIKI_ID and follow the resume hint.
match_rule: Identify unconditional resume advice for promptless archived Mjolnir sessions despite restoration requiring a user prompt.
near_misses: Unavailable native harnesses or ordinary live-session resume failures.
why_findable: The new recommendation and restore path are in this feature; snapshot_of explicitly requires a prompt.
notes: base is intro^; attribution inspected in saved fix and intro diffs. Marker may have been added after fix.

marker_text: // Hard-won: 7414cc74: updating the checked-out branch first staged added files as deletions.
defect: Restoration updates the checked-out branch ref before checking out the saved commit. HEAD advances while the index and working files remain at the old commit, so checkout of the now-current tip leaves committed additions staged as deletions.
location: mj-checkpoint/src/archive/git.rs, restore_git_snapshot, around line 1032 at intro
trigger: Restore a managed clone checkpoint with commits adding files beyond the destination clone tip.
match_rule: Identify saved-ref restoration before checkout as leaving HEAD inconsistent with index/worktree and producing missing files or staged deletions.
near_misses: Stash ordering, remote ref loss, or generic dirty-checkout warnings.
why_findable: Git update-ref and checkout ordering and the clone restore path are all present.
notes: base=intro^; history inspected read-only; evidence in restore-branch-before-checkout-intro.diff and restore-branch-before-checkout-fix.diff

marker_text: // Hard-won: 69fc70a7: terminal IDs were reused across Kimi connection restarts.
defect: Every registry starts its terminal counter at zero and emits term-1, term-2 without connection identity. A restarted ACP connection reuses IDs retained by the session transcript, attaching output to an earlier tool.
location: src/hel_terminal.rs, TerminalRegistry::create, around line 190 at intro
trigger: Create a terminal, restart the harness/connection, then create another terminal in the same session.
match_rule: Identify registry-local counter reset causing terminal ID collisions across reconnects and misassociation of persisted output.
near_misses: Counter overflow or collisions between concurrent creates in one registry.
why_findable: Registry lifetime is per connection and transcript association uses the terminal ID.
notes: base=intro^; history inspected read-only; evidence in terminal-id-reused-intro.diff and terminal-id-reused-fix.diff

marker_text: // Hard-won: 0b5375dc: Codex resume read only the generic effort key and lost its reasoning_effort selection.
defect: Restore reads only the generic effort key from archived configuration. Codex stores its selector under reasoning_effort, so native resume drops the accepted reasoning effort.
location: mj-checkpoint/src/checkpoint/restore.rs, restore_checkpoint_with_native_state, around line 57 at intro
trigger: Checkpoint a Codex conversation configured with reasoning_effort then resume it.
match_rule: Identify that archived reasoning_effort is ignored by the model/effort allowlist and the selected effort is lost on resume.
near_misses: Model ID mismatch or losing all settings when intentionally changing harness.
why_findable: The existing ACP selector interpretation knows the reasoning_effort alias, while restore reads a narrower key set.
notes: base=intro^; history inspected read-only; evidence in codex-effort-alias-lost-intro.diff and codex-effort-alias-lost-fix.diff

marker_text: // Hard-won: 21f785d: A resumed Codex session reverted an accepted model to the profile default.
defect: The accepted Codex model is pinned into the persisted supervisor environment only at worker startup. Models selected after startup never update that file; an in-worker bridge restart opens the resumed thread with the stale model/profile default.
location: mj-worker/src/worker_runtime/unix.rs, run_daemon, around line 288 at intro
trigger: Select a new Codex model after worker startup, then restart the bridge without replacing the worker.
match_rule: Identify that pinning once before persisting the supervisor spec fails to propagate subsequent accepted model changes to later bridge launches.
near_misses: The earlier defect of never pinning any model, or merely reasoning-effort restoration.
why_findable: The added startup-only pin and persisted supervisor reuse, together with mutable accepted configuration, expose the stale snapshot.
notes: base=intro^; history inspected read-only; evidence in stale-model-launch-spec-intro.diff and stale-model-launch-spec-fix.diff

marker_text: // Hard-won: e97c0266: a child obeyed an invisible handback reminder and stopped before finishing its task.
defect: The automatic reminder orders the child to hand back and stop whenever its turn ended without a report. A normally ended turn need not mean the assignment is finished, so the reminder makes unfinished work report completion instead of continuing.
location: mj-core/src/subagent.rs, HANDBACK_REMINDER_TEXT, around line 324 at intro
trigger: A child ends a turn with unfinished assigned work but without calling handback; the automatic reminder is sent.
match_rule: Identify unconditional handback-and-stop wording on turn completion as prematurely terminating unfinished assignments.
near_misses: Handback size limits, reminder duplication, or tool permission issues.
why_findable: The reminder text and report_state trigger on turn outcome rather than task completion are added together.
notes: base=intro^; history inspected read-only; evidence in handback-reminder-stops-work-intro.diff and handback-reminder-stops-work-fix.diff

marker_text: // Hard-won: 27e5da78: recovery returned valid-JSON records whose digest had been corrupted by a byte flip.
defect: Recover mode treats successfully parsed JSON as a recovered record without validating its digest. A byte flip that preserves JSON syntax is passed to the recovery visitor as fabricated data instead of being reported as corruption.

marker_text: // Hard-won: 38f041c03: a metadata-only capture whose only refs/mj ref was a dropped pin restored as a full snapshot.

location: mj-checkpoint/src/archive/git.rs, collect_git_metadata_snapshot, around line 200 at intro

notes: base=intro^; history inspected read-only; evidence in metadata-checkpoint-overwrites-checkout-intro.diff and metadata-checkpoint-overwrites-checkout-fix.diff

marker_text: // Hard-won: 131223a: sub-agent MCP calls returned accepted placeholders instead of their daemon result.
defect: The MCP socket handler returns immediately after enqueue, before the daemon completes the action. A first wait/list/spawn call therefore returns accepted with no result rather than the requested child result or ID; daemon results are delivered later as conversation input.
trigger: Invoke a new spawn_agent or wait_agents request while its daemon action has not yet been processed.
match_rule: Identify immediate enqueue acknowledgement being returned as the MCP tool result, so the caller does not receive the actual spawn/wait response through the tool call.
near_misses: Request ID collisions, persistence errors, or simply preferring asynchronous APIs.
why_findable: The socket reply contains accepted=true with result=None, while exposed tool contracts promise IDs/child results and daemon completion is separate.
notes: base=intro^; history inspected read-only; evidence in subagent-tool-placeholder-intro.diff and subagent-tool-placeholder-fix.diff

marker_text: // Hard-won: c82d9df3: an empty Claude session opened above an archive floor was mistaken for used history.
defect: The new history predicate treats every nonzero recovery floor as proof that the current native thread contains history. A moved/restored session can create a new native thread above that floor and never prompt it; the old archive cannot contain that new thread, but the predicate forbids recreating it when resume finds no rollout.
location: mj-worker/src/relay.rs, native_session_may_have_history, around line 1007 at intro
trigger: Move a session to a fresh Codex native thread above the restored archive floor, restart its worker before the first prompt, and resume the missing thread.
match_rule: Identify unconditional nonzero recovery-floor rejection as misclassifying a new unused thread opened after the floor and blocking its safe recreation.
